reviewers.summary: The added cases cover many inputs, but the test-side validator makes the new contract checks self-fulfilling and unable to detect production regressions.

findingList.message: The test duplicates the contract rules instead of verifying them through production validation, so it cannot detect when those production behaviors are absent or broken.

evidence.codePathTraced: AssertContract calls ValidateContract, which calls production Validate and then independently enforces the new scope, category, currency, and period rules in test code.
evidence.failureScenario: If production Validate accepts an out-of-set scope such as "E", ValidateContract still rejects it itself, so the test passes. Removing or breaking the production scope check would not make this test fail.

reviewers.summary: The named test runs under the build-and-gate job, but the duplicated test-only validation means its scope, category, currency, and timestamp cases do not prove production behavior.

findingList.message: The new cases assert several contract rules in a test-only validator rather than against production validation. They therefore pass even when DeploymentCostEvidence.Validate accepts invalid scope, category, currency, or period values, and do not verify those acceptance criteria.

evidence.codePathTraced: AssertContract calls the test-only ValidateContract helper, which calls evidence.Validate() and then applies its own scope, category, currency, timestamp, and period rules.
evidence.failureScenario: If production Validate() accepts scope "E", ValidateContract still throws using its duplicated scope check, so the test expecting rejection passes and does not catch the broken production behavior.

reviewers.summary: The added cases cover many inputs, but the test-local validator supplies the rules those cases assert. As written, the test does not reliably detect regressions in production validation.

findingList.message: The test duplicates the contract rules in test-local ValidateContract, so its cases can pass even when production validation is broken. Exercise the production validation path directly for the listed accepted and rejected values.

evidence.codePathTraced: AssertContract calls test-local ValidateContract, which calls evidence.Validate() and then independently implements the scope, category, label, currency, and period rules in the test file.
evidence.failureScenario: If production validation stops rejecting an out-of-set scope, the test still passes because ValidateContract rejects it itself. The named test therefore does not verify that the production record enforces these contract cases.
